notes:
Background: Enterprise insurer with heavy conversational + semantic search workloads across claims and customer support. Primary ask: reserved GPU pool planning across US regions with deterministic throughput guarantees and documented failover headroom.

Key quotes from CTO: "We need predictable latency at scale — not best-effort. If the east region is degraded, west must take 30% load within 60s."

Requirements summary (high-level):
- Workloads: customer chat (multitenant, PII scrubbed), semantic search over 2B claim documents (embeddings), model-based reranking for fraud alerts.
- Latency SLOs: p50 ~40-60ms token time for short replies; p95 <= 250ms end-to-end for 256-token prompts; p99 <= 400ms during steady-state.
- Throughput: baseline 120 concurrent RPS aggregate across regions for chat; expected daily peaks up to 420 RPS with 10x burst patterns during claims events.
- Capacity planning ask: reserved GPUs to cover baseline + 30% failover headroom per region; multi-region active-active preferred with warm standby per AZ.
- AZ spread: want pools distributed across at least 2 AZs per region to avoid single-AZ blast radius.
- Failover behaviour: automated weighted-failover routing + capacity-aware throttling; want rollback and canary for model rollouts.
- Models: prefer mix of 70B quantized variants for quality, auto-fallback to 13B quantized for capacity pressure.
- Cost sensitivity: medium-high — open to committed monthly/annual reserved capacity if unit economics predictable.
- Security: VPC-only control plane, KMS/HSM integration, full audit logging retention 1 year, SSO/SAML, data residency constraints for EU-stored backups.

Recent activity (bulleted timeline):
- 2026-01-28: Initial inbound from platform team; set up intro call.
- 2026-02-03: Discovery call (AE Sofia, SE Liam) — gathered traffic patterns and peak event examples.
- 2026-02-11: Architecture workshop (ff_20260211_ocy-call-9283) — sketched active-active across us-east1/us-west1 with AZ spread.
- 2026-02-20: Security questionnaire submitted; client requested KMS/HSM architecture diagram.
- 2026-02-25: POC scope defined: benchmark 70B quantized model at 256-token prompt, measure p95/p99 and throughput scaling; warm-failover test included (ff_20260225_arch-review-1147).
- 2026-03-01: Pricing deck shared and follow-up on reserved GPU SKU mix (drive:/decks/oceancrest-redwood-dedicated-proposal.pdf).

POC & technical asks:
- Provide GPU SKU recommendation mapping (e.g., 8x A100-80GB equiv per region for baseline, +3x reserved for AZ failover) and expected throughput numbers per SKU. They asked for a prescriptive worksheet.
- Run synthetic traffic sim matching their 10x burst profile and measure recovery time when removing 25% of capacity in region (failover test).
- Include quantization profile options and expected token/sec per model variant.
- Confirm autoscaling and burst policies for Dedicated pools; define warm vs cold capacity and billing implications.

Commercial & SLA negotiation notes:
- Procurement will push for a 99.95% availability SLA with credits; legal wants explicit failover RTO/RPO statements for multi-region.
- They prefer annual committed capacity with a right to adjust +/-20% at quarter boundaries.
- Pricing sensitivity around reserved vs burst pricing; interested in an amortized per-token blended rate for committed capacity.

Next steps (short, actionable):
- Deliver GPU sizing worksheet and estimated throughput table by 2026-03-05.
- Schedule joint SRE runbook review with their infra team (2-week window).
- Confirm SOW draft and procurement preferred payment terms (Sofia to coordinate).

Notes style: shorthand, call snippets, config-level asks included. Tracker: INFRA-2218 opened for POC infra reservations.
